Card text:

KNYFE deals each target 1 energy damage.

KNYFE may deal any target dealt damage this way an additional 1 energy damage.

It is unclear to me whether I am allowed to apply the second effect to multiple targets.  Can I, for example, hit everyone for 1 damage and then opt for all the non-hero targets to take an additional 1 energy damage.  Or is it the case that only one target amongst all those damaged can be selected for the additional damage?

If it is the former, then this card is okay (basically a weaker version of Haka's Rampage).  If it is the latter, then this card is complete garbage.

posts.name: Braithwhite
posts.cooked:
Step A- deal all targets 1 energy damage.  apply any buffs/resistances as needed.

Step B- You MAY deal any target that took damage from step A, 1 (one) energy damage, applying buffs/resistances as needed.  You can do this on a case by case basis.

 

You can absolutely do it to multiple targets.  it scales VERY well with damage multipliers (like parse/legacy/ra/her own focusing conduit blade), and is more forgiving than rampage or (potentially) oblivion.  it also works well with tricky cards like Twist the ether- KNYFE can have a LOT of fun with visionary.

I think that we are arguing the same exact point.  Let me re-phrase.

Hypersonic assault requires that everyone who takes damage gets the effect: cannot do damage.  

For incidental contact, everyone who takes damage from step A gets the effect: KNYFE may deal this target 1 energy damage.

For each effected (took damage) target (of step A), KNYFE makes the decision (on a case by case basis, predicated on whether or not they took damage in step A) of applying the secondary effect.  the secondary effect being that she MAY deal them 1 energy damage (or not, if that is what she decided to do).  

Basically, you see who gets hit from the first wave- and then you decide which of that set gets hit again.

Oh I remember long threads arguing over the proper way to play Hypersonic Assault. I have that ruling burned deep haha.

So, just to clarify the proper steps here:

Target A gets dealt 1 damage from Incidental Contact. If damage is dealt (HP lowered), that triggers the secondary effect. By common rule, consecutive triggers resolve from newest to oldest. Resolve the second effect from Incidental Contact for target A

Move to Target B. Repeat above.

Move to Target C. Repeat. and so on.

posts.name: Braithwhite
posts.cooked:
We're arguing about how to resolve the timing of the steps on the card.  In some cases, when an effect happens is absolutely critical.

Hypersonic assault (for instance) caused a debate, because there are targets that deal damage in retaliation, or in response to cards being destroyed (such as the chairman dealing damage when being hit, or the Matriarch hitting when birds are destroyed).

The debate centered around WHEN the secondary effect (targets can't deal damage) happened- did it happen as soon as a target was dealt damage?  did it happen after ALL targets were dealt damage?

If you resolved the entire card one target at a time (which was the eventual ruling), then you could pull off a lot of fun tricks like hitting the Matriarch first (so that she couldn't deal damage), and then taking out her entire army of birds with the rest of Hypersonic Assault.

 

In response to your question:  

you can apply the additional damage to multiple targets.  You do this one target at a time- deal a target 1 energy, then if it took damage, you decide if you are going to deal it 1 more energy damage.  Once this is accomplished for one target, move on to the next target.
